s.note: the bruschetta Julie makes to unwind
s.how: Toast slices of a ciabatta and rub with a cut garlic clove. Dice 4 ripe tomatoes, salt and leave 10 minutes. Mix with torn basil and 2 tbsp olive oil and pile on just before serving.

s.note: a French classic to warm up the kitchen
s.how: Boil 125ml water with 50g butter, beat in 75g flour and cook a minute. Cool slightly, beat in 2 eggs one at a time, then 80g grated gruyère and nutmeg. Pipe rounds and bake at 200C for 20 minutes. Bon appétit.

m.note: the dish that defines the project
m.how: Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck and 150g bacon lardons. Add 2 carrots, an onion and garlic, then 750ml red wine, 250ml stock and herbs. Braise at 160C for 3 hours. Glaze 12 pearl onions and 250g mushrooms in butter and stir through.

w.note: a classic French chocolate almond cake from the book
w.how: Melt 125g dark chocolate with 100g butter. Beat 3 yolks with 100g sugar, add the chocolate, then fold in 60g almond meal and 30g flour. Fold in 3 whipped whites. Bake at 180C for 25 minutes. Glaze with 60g chocolate melted with butter.

d.n: Burgundy kir with crème de cassis
d.how: Chill a 750ml bottle of dry white Burgundy or chardonnay for 2 hours. Pour 15ml crème de cassis into each of four wine glasses. Top slowly with 120ml cold wine so it blends from the bottom. Drop a blackberry into each glass and serve before the bourguignon. Pour red with the main.
